title: Passport Apply Online 2026: e-Passport, Tatkal, Fees, PV
meta_description: Passport apply online 2026: every new passport is a chip e-Passport. Fees Rs 1,500-4,000, tatkal without gazetted certificate, ECR rules, Annexure J, PSK steps.

hero.one_liner: Apply at passportindia.gov.in and you now get a chip-enabled e-Passport. Fees start at ₹1,500, tatkal arrives in days, and the 2025-26 rule changes matter more than most guides admit.

sections.heading: Passport in 2026: What You Are Actually Applying For
content: A passport application in 2026 runs through Passport Seva 2.0, the rebuilt system that went live on May 26, 2025. The process is online-first: form and payment on passportindia.gov.in, one physical visit for biometrics, then police verification.
The document you receive has changed too. Every new passport issued now is a chip-enabled e-Passport, and three rule changes from 2025 affect documents, addresses, and what gets printed inside.

This guide covers the full route: fresh application, tatkal, renewal, minors, ECR status, and the annexures that confuse everyone. Fees have not changed, starting at ₹1,500 for a fresh 36-page booklet.

sections.heading: Your Next Passport Is an e-Passport
content: You do not choose an e-Passport, you simply get one. Since the nationwide rollout under Passport Seva 2.0, every fresh and reissued passport carries an embedded RFID chip holding your photo and biometric data to ICAO standards.
Spot it by the small gold chip symbol on the front cover. The application process, fees, and documents are the same as before, so there is no separate e-Passport application or extra charge.
The practical win is e-gates. Chip passports work with automated immigration gates in the UAE, Singapore, much of Europe, and Australia, cutting queues from 20-30 minutes to under 5.
Your existing non-chip booklet stays valid until its printed expiry date. There is no requirement to upgrade early, though frequent flyers often renew ahead of time just for the chip.

sections.heading: Old booklet? It stays valid
sections.content:
Passports issued before the e-Passport rollout remain valid until expiry. Immigration accepts both formats everywhere.

Renew early only if e-gate access is worth it to you. The renewal fee is the same ₹1,500 either way.

sections.heading: The 2025 Rule Changes Nobody Told You About
content: The Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2025, notified on February 24, 2025, changed three things that affect real applications. Most older guides still miss all three.

Date of birth: anyone born on or after October 1, 2023 must submit a birth certificate from the Registrar of Births and Deaths or municipal authority, and nothing else is accepted. Those born earlier can still use a 10th marksheet, PAN, driving licence, voter ID, or service record, but Aadhaar no longer appears in the DOB list.

Address privacy: your residential address is no longer printed on the last page. Immigration officers read it from a barcode instead, which also means your home address is not visible to anyone who handles your passport.
Parents' names no longer print on the passport, a change made for children of single parents and estranged families. The application form still collects them, they just stay off the booklet.
Covers are now colour-coded: navy blue for ordinary citizens, white for government officials on duty, and red for diplomats.

sections.heading: ECR vs Non-ECR: The Stamp That Can Stop You at the Airport
content: ECR means Emigration Check Required. If your passport carries ECR status, you need emigration clearance from the Protector of Emigrants before flying to 18 notified countries for work, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, and Malaysia.

Who gets ECR: applicants who have not passed Class 10. Everyone who has passed matriculation or higher automatically gets non-ECR (ECNR) status, and so do all passport holders above 50 and children below 18.
Check your own status on page 2 of the passport. If nothing about ECR is printed, you are non-ECR, and an explicit ECR stamp means clearance applies.
Upgrading from ECR to non-ECR is a reissue: apply for a passport reissue with your 10th pass certificate as proof, and the new booklet comes without the stamp.
Tourist travel to ECR countries does not need clearance, only employment does. Airlines check this at boarding for work visas, which is where unaware workers get offloaded.

sections.heading: Step 1: Register & Apply Online on Passport Seva

steps.title: Visit passportindia.gov.in - Passport Seva Portal
steps.description: Go to official Ministry of External Affairs passport portal. First-time users: Click 'Register' to create account with email and password. Existing users: Click 'Login'.

steps.title: Click 'Apply for Fresh Passport' or 'Re-issue of Passport'
steps.description: Choose: (1) Fresh Passport → for first-time applicants, (2) Re-issue of Passport → for renewal or changes to existing passport. Each has its own form.

steps.title: Select Normal or Tatkal processing
steps.description: Fresh Passport: Choose Normal (30 days, ₹1,500) or Tatkal (1-3 days, ₹3,500). Renewal: Can also choose Normal or Tatkal (Tatkal renewal less common but available for urgent travel).

steps.title: Select 36-page or 60-page booklet
steps.description: 36-page: Standard, cheaper, sufficient for most people (valid 10 years, approximately 32-page capacity for visa stamps). 60-page: For frequent travelers, more visa space. Difference: ₹500 (36-page ₹1,500 vs 60-page ₹2,000).

steps.title: Fill online application form
steps.description: Very detailed form - takes 30-45 minutes. Enter: Full name (as on Aadhaar), date of birth, gender, parents' names (father + mother), present address, permanent address (if different), occupation, educational qualification, emergency contact, mother tongue, previous passport details (if any).

steps.title: Answer security questions about your address history
steps.description: The form asks: Where did you live in the last 1-3 years? Any frequent address changes trigger additional verification. Be accurate - lies here can lead to police investigation.

steps.title: Select Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) nearest to you
steps.description: Choose: Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) = dedicated passport center, OR Post Office Passport Seva Kendra (POPSK) = passport services at select post offices. Both process identically. Choose whichever is nearest to your location.

steps.title: Upload photo and signature
steps.description: Upload a recent colour photo on a plain white background and a scanned signature, within the size limits the portal shows at the upload step. This upload is for records, the final passport photo and biometrics are captured live at the PSK. A blurry or shadowed photo still gets flagged, so use a clean, well-lit image.

steps.title: Upload identity and address documents (PDF/JPEG, max 500KB each)
steps.description: Identity proof: Aadhaar card (best), Voter ID, Driving License, or PAN card - scan both sides. Address proof: Aadhaar (best), Utility bill (within 3 months), Bank statement, Passport, Voter ID. Date of birth proof: Birth certificate (for births after 26/01/1989, this is MANDATORY), 10th marksheet, Aadhaar, Passport. Scan all documents clearly - blurry scans cause rejection.

steps.title: Upload guardianship documents (if applicable)
steps.description: For minors: Birth certificate is mandatory. Parental consent letter (letter from parents confirming they consent to passport, on plain paper, signed by both). Marriage certificate (if married and name changed). Divorce decree (if previously divorced and name reverted).

steps.title: Review all information before submission
steps.description: CRITICAL STEP: Review all details carefully. Name, DOB, parents' names, address - all must match uploaded documents exactly. Mismatches cause rejections. Recheck 2-3 times before proceeding.

steps.title: Pay fee online
steps.description: Fees: Fresh 36-page: ₹1,500, Fresh 60-page: ₹2,000, Renewal 36-page: ₹1,500, Renewal 60-page: ₹2,000, Tatkal 36-page: ₹3,500, Tatkal 60-page: ₹4,000. Pay via: Net banking (all banks), Debit card, Credit card, or SBI Challan (if preferred, pay at bank and upload receipt). Online payment is instant and gives you receipt immediately.

steps.title: Download application receipt
steps.description: After payment, system generates 'Application Reference Number' (ARN) and allows download of application receipt (PDF). SAVE THIS RECEIPT - you'll need to show it at PSK appointment.

steps.title: Book appointment at Passport Seva Kendra (PSK)
steps.description: After online payment, book an appointment at your chosen PSK or POPSK from the calendar of available slots. Tatkal slots are released separately and usually 1-3 days out. If your nearest PSK shows no slots for weeks, check POPSKs in the district before waiting.

steps.title: Prepare documents for PSK visit
steps.description: Bring: (1) Application receipt (printed), (2) Original Aadhaar + color photocopy, (3) Original address proof + photocopy (utility bill/bank statement), (4) Birth certificate (original), (5) For minors: original parental consent letter, (6) For name change: marriage certificate or deed poll, (7) Appointment confirmation (printed or on mobile), (8) Any other original documents uploaded.

steps.title: Visit PSK on appointment date
steps.description: Reach 10 minutes early (appointments are strict, arriving late may cancel slot). Carry all documents. PSK process: (1) Token number issued, (2) Counter A: Document verification and cross-checking with uploaded scans, (3) Counter B: Biometric capture - photo taken at PSK (overwriting uploaded photo), fingerprints (all 10 fingers), and signature captured on tablet, (4) Counter C: Final verification and confirmation. Total time at PSK: 1-3 hours.

steps.title: No need for police interview at PSK
steps.description: Police verification happens AFTER you leave PSK (for fresh passports). You don't interact with police at PSK. Police verification is done at your home address afterward (officer visits, sometimes both times or just once).

steps.title: Police verification for fresh passport applicants
steps.description: After your PSK visit, the passport office sends the case to the police station covering your application address. An officer visits the address, confirms you live there, and may ask neighbours or the landlord. This applies to fresh applications; renewals with unchanged address often skip it.

steps.title: If police verification fails
steps.description: Usually happens if: (1) You listed wrong address, (2) You're not present when officer visits (ask to reschedule), (3) Neighbors deny knowing you (common in large apartments). Contact your local police station to clarify. If address is correct and you're cooperative, it ALWAYS passes eventually - just may take additional time.

steps.title: Passport printing
steps.description: After police verification approval, your passport is printed. This takes 5-10 days from verification clearance.

steps.title: Delivery via Speed Post
steps.description: Printed passport is dispatched via India Post Speed Post to your registered address (the address in your application). Delivery takes 2-5 days depending on location. Track delivery at indiapost.gov.in or the tracking number provided via SMS.

steps.title: Receive passport at home
steps.description: Passport arrives in a sealed envelope. You sign receipt. Passport is now valid for: 10 years (for adults), 5 years (for minors). Check validity date inside the booklet.

sections.heading: Tatkal Passport: How It Really Works Now
content: Tatkal costs ₹2,000 over the normal fee and exists for genuine urgency: a job joining date, a visa interview, a medical emergency abroad. You select Tatkal in the same online form, no separate application.

The rule most guides get wrong: the gazetted officer Verification Certificate (old Annexure F) has not been required since December 16, 2019, under G.S.R. 939(E). Adults submit any three documents from the acceptable list, minors any two.

That list is ordinary paperwork: Aadhaar, voter ID, PAN, driving licence, 10th certificate, bank passbook, and similar. If an agent tells you to hunt down a gazetted officer, they are working from pre-2019 rules or inventing a service fee.
Speed: once your status shows Granted, the passport dispatches on the third working day, without waiting for police verification. Verification happens after issuance instead of before.
Tatkal is not open to everyone. Pending criminal cases, prior deportation, and adverse police records push you to the normal queue, and the passport office holds final discretion.
If travel is more than three weeks away, normal processing usually gets there in time. Tatkal is for real deadlines, not agent upselling.

sections.heading: Tatkal myth check
sections.content:
No gazetted officer certificate, no proof of emergency, and no flight ticket are required for Tatkal. Three listed documents and the extra fee are the whole requirement.

Anyone charging you to arrange an Annexure F is selling a document abolished in 2019.

sections.heading: Police Verification: What Happens and How to Prepare
content: After the PSK visit, your file goes to the police station covering your application address. An officer visits your home, checks that you live there, and asks neighbours or the landlord to confirm.
Keep three things handy: the application receipt, your rent agreement if renting, and the landlord's phone number. Tenants fail verification more often than owners purely on reachability.
Timing is usually 7-15 days after the PSK visit for normal applications. For Tatkal, verification happens after the passport is already issued.
The officer visits during working hours, which is exactly when you are out. Share your phone number at the local station and ask for a call before the visit.
If nobody has come after 15 days, walk into the station with your application reference number. A pending file often moves the same day you ask about it.
A pending criminal case does not automatically block a passport, but it needs court permission. Submit that proactively rather than letting the file stall.

sections.heading: Passport Annexures Explained (J, D, C, B)
content: Annexure J is the one everyone searches for. Since April 2025 it replaces the marriage certificate for adding a spouse's name: a joint declaration signed by both spouses, with a self-attested joint photograph, names, address, and ID numbers.
Couples from states where marriages often go unregistered were the reason for the change. Fill it, paste the joint photo, both sign with place and date, and carry ID copies to the PSK.
Annexure D is the parents' declaration for a minor's passport, signed by both. When one parent cannot or will not consent, Annexure C covers the single-parent situation.
Annexure B is the identity certificate route for government employees, used alongside or instead of a departmental NOC.
Annexure F no longer exists as a Tatkal requirement, abolished in 2019. Removing or changing a spouse's name still needs legal proof: divorce decree, death certificate, or a fresh declaration.

sections.heading: Renewal and Reissue
content: Renewal is a reissue application at passportindia.gov.in, and you can file up to one year before expiry or within three years after. The fee matches a fresh application, ₹1,500 normal.
Police verification is often waived on renewal if your address is unchanged and the expiring passport had a clean record. That makes renewals meaningfully faster than fresh applications.
Lost or stolen passport: file a police report first, then apply for reissue at the higher lost-passport fee. Verification is mandatory again for lost cases.
Damaged booklet: carry the damaged passport itself to the PSK with a reissue application. Name changes after marriage go the same reissue route, with the marriage certificate or Annexure J.
Every reissue you receive now is a chip e-Passport, whatever your old booklet was.

sections.heading: Passports for Minors and Newborns
content: A minor's passport costs ₹1,000 and runs 5 years or until age 18, whichever comes first. Both parents sign Annexure D, and the child's photo is captured at the PSK, newborns included.

The 2025 birth certificate rule bites here first: any child born on or after October 1, 2023 must have a municipal birth certificate, with no substitute documents. Get the certificate before starting the passport form, not after.
Bring the child to the PSK appointment, since biometrics and photo happen in person. Infants are photographed lying on a white sheet if they cannot sit.
At 18 the minor passport does not convert. The holder applies fresh as an adult with their own documents and gets the full 10-year booklet.

sections.heading: POPSK: The Shortcut Small Towns Should Use
content: POPSKs are passport counters inside post offices, over 450 of them, built for districts without a full PSK. The process is identical: same portal, same fees, same biometrics.
The advantage is queues. City PSK appointments can run weeks out while a POPSK 30 km away has slots this week, and the portal shows both when you pick a centre.
Find them under Locate Passport Seva Centre on passportindia.gov.in. Check the working days before travelling, since some POPSK counters operate only 2-3 days a week.

sections.heading: Use POPSK instead of PSK - shorter queues, same service
sections.content:
If your nearest PSK is booked out for weeks, check the POPSKs in your district. There are 450+ across India, many in smaller towns with far shorter queues.

The service and fees are identical to a full PSK. Pick whichever centre has the earliest slot.

sections.heading: Don't use third-party websites or agents
sections.content:
passportindia.gov.in is the only legitimate application portal. Lookalike domains charge ₹1,000-5,000 for a form you can fill yourself in 30 minutes.

No agent can speed up processing. Book directly and keep your login details private.

sections.text: 14 crore Indian passports are in circulation - but 90 crore+ Indians still don't have one. The passport application process takes 30 minutes online and one PSK visit. Total cost: Rs 1,500. If you have any future plans involving international travel - for work, education, medical treatment, or even just the option to travel - apply now. A passport in hand opens doors that you can't predict today.

sections.heading: Official Sources & References
sections.content:
Passport Seva 2.0 and e-Passport rollout: Ministry of External Affairs announcements, 2025-26. Rule changes: Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2025, notified February 24, 2025.

Tatkal documents: G.S.R. 939(E) of December 2019, per the official Passport Seva FAQ. Fees and slots are set by passportindia.gov.in, verify before paying.

faqs.question: How long does a passport take to arrive in 2026?
faqs.answer:
Normal: roughly 15-30 days after the PSK visit including police verification, plus 2-5 days of Speed Post. Tatkal: dispatch on the third working day after status shows Granted.

Renewals with unchanged address often skip verification and land in 7-15 days. Track everything on passportindia.gov.in with your file number.

faqs.question: Is the e-Passport mandatory? Is my old passport still valid?
faqs.answer:
Every new and reissued passport is a chip e-Passport, so there is nothing to opt into. Your old booklet stays valid until its expiry date.

The chip brings e-gate access at many foreign airports. Renew early only if that matters to you.

faqs.question: What is Annexure J for passport?
faqs.answer:
Annexure J is a joint declaration signed by both spouses, with a self-attested joint photograph, used to add a spouse's name without a marriage certificate. It has been accepted since April 2025.

Fill names, address, and ID numbers, both sign with place and date, and carry ID copies to the PSK.

faqs.question: What is ECR and non-ECR in a passport?
faqs.answer:
ECR means Emigration Check Required: workers who have not passed Class 10 need emigration clearance before taking jobs in 18 notified countries like the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Non-ECR (ECNR) applies automatically to 10th-pass applicants, everyone above 50, and minors.

Check page 2 of your passport. To remove ECR, apply for reissue with your 10th certificate.

faqs.question: Can I apply for a passport without Aadhaar?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Aadhaar is the most convenient identity and address proof, but voter ID, driving licence, utility bills, and bank statements also work.

Note that under the 2025 rules Aadhaar does not count as date-of-birth proof, so you need a separate DOB document either way.

faqs.question: Who can apply for a tatkal passport, and is a gazetted certificate needed?
faqs.answer:
Any applicant can opt for Tatkal by paying ₹2,000 extra, except those with pending criminal cases, deportation history, or adverse police records. The gazetted officer certificate (Annexure F) was abolished in December 2019.

Adults submit any three documents from the acceptable list, minors any two. Dispatch happens on the third working day after Granted, before police verification.

faqs.question: How much does an Indian passport cost?
faqs.answer:
Fresh or renewal: ₹1,500 for 36 pages, ₹2,000 for 60 pages. Tatkal adds ₹2,000 on top.

Minor passports cost ₹1,000, and lost or damaged reissues run ₹3,000-3,500. Seniors above 60 and children under 8 get a 10% rebate on fresh applications, payable online by UPI, card, or net banking.

faqs.question: The form asks: have you ever applied for a passport but not been issued one?
faqs.answer:
Answer yes only if you previously submitted a passport application that was refused, closed, or never completed. A plain first-time applicant answers no.

Answering wrongly here counts as suppression of information and can get the application refused, so read it carefully rather than clicking through.

faqs.question: Can I apply for a passport anywhere in India?
faqs.answer:
You apply under the passport office that covers your present residential address, because police verification happens at that address. You cannot file in your hometown while living in another city.

Within your region you can pick any PSK or POPSK that is convenient, including one in a neighbouring district.

faqs.question: Police verification failed. What now?
faqs.answer:
Most failures are reachability: wrong address, nobody home, or neighbours who could not confirm you. Contact the local police station with your file number and request a fresh visit at a fixed time.

If the address itself was wrong, you may need to reapply with the correct one. Keep your rent agreement and landlord's number ready the second time.

faqs.question: What is the file number in a passport?
faqs.answer:
The file number is the reference under which your application was processed, printed inside the passport and shown in every status update. Visa forms for some countries ask for it.

You can retrieve it anytime by logging into passportindia.gov.in, where it appears against your application.

faqs.question: How do I apply for a passport for a newborn baby?
faqs.answer:
Apply as a minor application: ₹1,000 fee, 5-year validity, both parents signing Annexure D. A municipal birth certificate is compulsory for any child born on or after October 1, 2023.

The baby must come to the PSK, where infants are photographed lying on a white sheet. Carry both parents' IDs and passports if available.

faqs.question: Can I hold two passports?
faqs.answer:
No, one person may hold only one valid Indian passport, and a found old passport must be surrendered at the PSK. Holding two invites penal action under the Passports Act.

The old booklet you submit at renewal is cancelled and returned if it carries valid visas.

faqs.question: What is the passport validity, and when should I renew?
faqs.answer:
Ten years for adults, five years for minors or until they turn 18, whichever comes first. You can renew up to one year before expiry or within three years after.

Many countries require six months of remaining validity to grant a visa, so renew well before the printed date if you travel.

disclaimer: Passport fees, processing times, and procedures as per Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) as of March 2026. MEA may update procedures, documents, or fees. Always check passportindia.gov.in for latest updates before applying.
